primary_audit_findings.exact_lines: Lines 30-32, 142-144, 203-214 (and M14 instantiation at rtl_v3/taalas_hc1_layer_tile.sv Lines 245-247)
standard_or_literature_reference: Rabaey, Chandrakasan & Nikolic, Digital Integrated Circuits (2nd Ed., Ch. 11: Dynamic NOR/NAND ROM Precharge-Evaluate Timing)
Weste & Harris, CMOS VLSI Design (4th Ed., Ch. 12: Mask-Programmed ROM Bitline Contention Prevention)

primary_audit_findings.current_rtl_behavior: Line 143 defines mux_read_fire = (!effective_sleep) && ((bist_state_q == BIST_SCAN) || (cs_en && precharge_en && sa_en)), and Line 205 latches rdata_q only when (cs_en && precharge_en && sa_en) are all simultaneously 1'b1. Furthermore, M14 (taalas_hc1_layer_tile.sv Lines 245-247) ties .cs_en(rom_cs_en), .precharge_en(rom_cs_en), and .sa_en(rom_cs_en) together.
primary_audit_findings.root_cause_and_physical_impact: In a physical TSMC N6 Via-2 Mask ROM array, bitline PMOS precharge (pulling bitlines to VDD) and wordline NMOS evaluation (discharging programmed Via-2 bitlines to GND) must be strictly mutually exclusive. Asserting wordline evaluation while bitline PMOS precharge is active creates a direct VDD-to-GND static crowbar current path across up to 512 bitlines (~76.8 mA peak DC contention per macro), causing bitline voltage divider contention, sense-amp read corruption, and Via-2 electromigration.
primary_audit_findings.stage23_required_rtl_fix: Add a dedicated hardware bitline-precharge vs. wordline-evaluation safety interlock in M01: (1) support non-overlapping precharge/evaluate operation and an explicit contention interlock that gates wordline decoding whenever active PMOS precharge contention is detected, (2) export a contention_fault_o diagnostic flag, and (3) add inline formal SVA property PROP_M1_NO_BL_WL_CONTENTION proving wordline assertion and active bitline pull-up never overlap.

primary_audit_findings.exact_lines: Lines 47-50, 122-167, 185-188, 243, 270-298 (and M14 integration at rtl_v3/taalas_hc1_layer_tile.sv Lines 324-330, 374-383)
standard_or_literature_reference: Open Compute Project (OCP) Microscaling Formats (MX) Specification v1.0 (Rouhani et al. 2023), Section 5.2 & Table 2: E8M0 Shared Scale Encoding (8'hFF = NaN)
IEEE Std 754-2019 Section 6.2 (Quiet NaN Propagation) & Section 4.3.1 (Round-to-Nearest-Even Subnormal Normalization)
primary_audit_findings.current_rtl_behavior: While Stage 10 patched fp32_out_o (Lines 186, 272-273) to output 32'h7FC0_0000 when w_e8 == 8'hFF or act_e8m0_i == 8'hFF, four compliance gaps remain: (1) in baseline rtl/taalas_mxfp4_hc2_mac_lane.sv, E8M0 == 8'hFF was treated as numeric exponent 255 (2^+128); (2) in rtl_v3/taalas_mxfp4_hc2_mac_lane.sv, nan_flag_q (Line 243) is internal-only and not exported on the module port list, while dot_int16_o and exp_comb_o (Lines 188, 291-292) still output raw arithmetic values (Ew + Ex - 256 = +254) during NaN scale events; (3) M14 (taalas_hc1_layer_tile.sv Lines 376-378) consumes mxfp4_dot_int16 directly in HC2 mode while ignoring mxfp4_fp32_out and NaN scale flags, silently propagating corrupted integer sums on E8M0=8'hFF; (4) normalize_int16_exp_to_fp32 (Line 157) truncates subnormal mantissas via right-shift without IEEE-754 Round-to-Nearest-Even (RNE) sticky/guard rounding.
primary_audit_findings.root_cause_and_physical_impact: Downstream integer/fixed-point consumers (such as M14's dequantizer mux) bypass fp32_out_o and ingest dot_int16_o directly, violating OCP MX v1.0 Section 5.2 which mandates that an E8M0 == 8'hFF shared scale must invalidate the entire block inner product across all output representations.
primary_audit_findings.stage23_required_rtl_fix: In M03: (1) export nan_scale_flag_o[NUM_LANES-1:0] as a primary output port, (2) clamp/zero dot_int16_o and force canonical exponent code on NaN scale so integer consumers cannot ingest unmasked garbage, (3) implement RNE guard/round/sticky rounding on subnormal shifts in normalize_int16_exp_to_fp32, and (4) propagate NaN saturation handling in M14.

standard_or_literature_reference: M. Y. Hsiao (1970), 'A Class of Optimal Minimum Odd-Weight-Column SEC-DED Codes', IBM Journal of Research and Development 14(4):395-401
R. W. Hamming (1950), 'Error Detecting and Error Correcting Codes', Bell System Technical Journal 29(2):147-160
JEDEC JESD79-5 On-Die ECC & High-Reliability Server SRAM [72,64] Hsiao SECDED Specification
primary_audit_findings.current_rtl_behavior: M05 (Lines 125-149), M18 (Lines 91-114), and H1 (Lines 106-131) implement a standard non-Hsiao Extended Hamming [72,64] code that maps data bits i in [0..63] to consecutive non-power-of-2 integers in [3..71] (which include even-weight columns 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12, 15, ..., 63) and computes overall parity serially as p_overall = (^d_in) ^ (^p_hamming). Crucially, in the syndrome decoder (M05 Lines 176-186, H1 Lines 157-164, M18 Lines 140-149), whenever total_parity == 1'b1, the decoder unconditionally asserts sec_flag = 1'b1 and ded_flag = 1'b0—even when syndrome_7b >= 7'd72 (which corresponds to no valid single-bit column in [0..71] and occurs on 3-bit adjacent MBU faults!). Additionally, H1's diagnostic fault injector (Lines 46, 241-243) only accepts a 6-bit err_inj_bit_i[5:0], making it impossible to inject faults into the 8 ECC parity bits [71:64].
primary_audit_findings.root_cause_and_physical_impact: First, standard Extended Hamming requires a deeper serial XOR cascade for bit 71 (p_overall depends on p_hamming[6:0]) compared to an optimal odd-weight-column Hsiao [72,64] generator matrix where every data column has odd weight (3 or 5) and all 8 check bits have balanced XOR trees. Second, setting sec_flag = 1'b1 whenever total_parity == 1'b1 without checking that syndrome_7b matches a valid codeword column (or power-of-2 check bit) causes 43.75% of odd-weight multi-bit upsets (syndrome_7b in [72..127]) to be silently misclassified as 'corrected' (SEC) while outputting corrupted data without raising ded_err_o!
primary_audit_findings.stage23_required_rtl_fix: Upgrade M05, M18, and H1 to: (1) verify valid column syndrome membership (syndrome_match_valid) so any odd-parity fault with an unmapped syndrome (syndrome_7b >= 7'd72) is flagged as an uncorrectable multi-bit fault (ded_flag = 1'b1, sec_flag = 1'b0) rather than a false SEC, (2) support optimal odd-weight-column Hsiao [72,64] parity checks, and (3) widen H1 fault injection to cover all 72 codeword bits.

primary_audit_findings.current_rtl_behavior: Four mathematical discrepancies exist in M08 and its M14 integration: (1) M08's phase-step ROM (Lines 63-91) only indexes 32 frequency bands (5-bit band_id = {pair_chunk_idx_i[1:0], 3'(p)} at Line 227, dropping pair_chunk_idx_i[2]), whereas Llama-3.1 head_dim = 128 has 64 complex frequency bands (i in 0..63); (2) for long-wavelength bands 22..31, rom_omega_base (Line 88) clamps all frequencies to the identical constant 16'd1 due to 16-bit phase truncation before multiplication, and Line 229 multiplies only token_pos_i[15:0] * omega_step (dropping bit 16 of token_pos_i and losing sub-LSB fractional phase precision across 128K context); (3) rom_omega_ntk_scaled (Lines 95-109) approximates Llama-3.1's smooth piecewise ramp (1 - gamma)*omega/8 + gamma*omega with a coarse 2-step shift (0.75x and 0.25x); (4) in M14 (Line 477), u_kv_cache_mgr receives unrotated qkv_vec_q[63:0] as k_vec_in_i instead of RoPE-rotated keys.
primary_audit_findings.root_cause_and_physical_impact: In 128K-context Llama-3.1 inference, clamping bands 22..63 to identical phase steps and truncating sub-LSB frequencies before multiplying by the 17-bit token position m destroys long-range relative position discrimination beyond 4K tokens, while bypassing RoPE on Key vectors in M14 breaks Q-K relative rotational invariance.
primary_audit_findings.stage23_required_rtl_fix: Upgrade M08 to: (1) full 64-band (6-bit band_id = {pair_chunk_idx_i[2:0], 3'(p)}) high-precision Q0.24 / 24-bit fractional phase-step ROM tables for both base theta=500,000 and exact Llama-3.1 piecewise smooth NTK scaling so (token_pos_i[16:0] * omega_u24) >> 8 preserves exact phase across all 64 bands and 131,072 positions, and (2) connect RoPE-rotated Key vectors into M14's KV-cache append path.

standard_or_literature_reference: Milakov & Gimelshein (2018), 'Online normalizer calculation for softmax', arXiv:1805.02867

High-Speed Multiplierless CSD Base-2 Softmax Identity: exp(x) = 2^(x * log2(e)), log2(e) = 1.44269504 ~= 1 + 2^-1 - 2^-4 + 2^-8 = 1.44140625
primary_audit_findings.current_rtl_behavior: Two severe arithmetic bugs were introduced in M09 during Stage 12 bitwidth-reduction edits: (1) At Line 176, eff_scale_s9 = (scale_log2e_q8_8_i == 16'd0) ? 9'sd46 : $signed(scale_log2e_q8_8_i[8:0]) slices the lower 9 bits as a signed two's-complement integer. When scale_log2e_q8_8_i is driven with standard Q8.8 log2(e) = 16'd369 (1.4414 in Q8.8, binary 9'b1_0111_0001), bit 8 is 1'b1, so $signed(scale_log2e_q8_8_i[8:0]) evaluates to NEGATIVE -143 (-0.5586), inverting the sign of all Q*K^T attention logits! (2) At Lines 274, 279-281, and 294-298, Stage 12 truncated alpha_q15, beta_q15, and inv_l_q15 to 6 fractional bits (alpha_q15[15:9], beta_q15[15:9]) for the value accumulator run_acc_q while accumulating beta_q15 in full 15-bit precision in run_denom_q (Line 274: + 25'(beta_q15)), causing any token with exp2 weight < 1/64 to contribute to the denominator while contributing 0 to the numerator!
primary_audit_findings.root_cause_and_physical_impact: Slicing [8:0] as signed limits positive Q8.8 scale factors to < 1.0 (max 255/256 = 0.996), breaking standalone log2(e) = 1.4427 scaling; meanwhile, mismatched Q15 denominator accumulation vs. Q6 numerator accumulation biases attention outputs toward zero on long sequences.
primary_audit_findings.stage23_required_rtl_fix: In M09: (1) implement dedicated multiplierless CSD log2(e) scaling (x + (x >>> 1) - (x >>> 4) + (x >>> 8)) combined with unsigned/full-range 16-bit Q8.8 scale multiplication so scale_log2e_q8_8_i up to 16'h7FFF never sign-inverts, and (2) align numerator and denominator rescaling precision so online softmax preserves exact probability conservation (sum of weights == 1.0).

primary_audit_findings.current_rtl_behavior: In H3 (Lines 108-129 and 148-194): (1) H3 lacks per-expert load-balancing bias registers/inputs b_e and does not separate biased routing scores s'_{e,t} = s_{e,t} + b_e (used strictly for Top-K tournament selection) from unbiased affinity scores s_{e,t} (used for gating weight normalization g_{e,t} = s_{e,t} / sum_{j in TopK} s_{j,t}); (2) at Lines 124-127, instead of applying true E8M0 exponent scaling to the MXFP4 dot product dot_sum, H3 XOR-folds w_e8, act_e8m0_i, and token_id_i into a synthetic 3-bit hash (scale_shift) added to dot_sum.
primary_audit_findings.root_cause_and_physical_impact: Without DeepSeek-V3/R1's decoupled auxiliary-loss-free bias s'_{e,t} = s_{e,t} + b_e, MoE routing either suffers from expert routing collapse on skewed token distributions or distorts expert gating weights by injecting load-balancing bias directly into the token feature linear combination.
primary_audit_findings.stage23_required_rtl_fix: Upgrade H3 to: (1) support DeepSeek-V3/R1 auxiliary-loss-free load-balancing bias vector (expert_bias_i / internal dynamic bias update table) where Top-K tournament selection compares biased scores s'_{e} = s_e + b_e while Q8.8 gating weight normalization uses the unbiased affinity scores s_e, and (2) replace the synthetic XOR scale_shift at Lines 124-127 with arithmetic E8M0 relative exponent scaling.
